title: Rangers Goalie Shesterkin Sidelined 1-2 Weeks with Upper-Body Injury
text:
Igor Shesterkin ⁤is out ‌1-2 weeks for the New ‍York Rangers⁢ with an ⁢ upper-body injury . The goalie started⁢ Friday and made ⁣23 saves ⁤in a 3-2 loss to the‌ Pittsburgh Penguins at Madison Square Garden. ⁢He stayed down on the ice after ‍a ​net-front scramble late in the first period and‌ the Rangers’ trainer came out to check ‌on him, but Shesterkin stayed in ​the ‌game.
Shesterkin is 18-19-2 with a 2.87 goals-against average, a .906 save percentage and three shutouts in 39 games this season. Jonathan Quick made 22 saves for New York in a 4-3 win at the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday, its last game before the 4 Nations Face-Off (Feb. 12-20). The Rangers will return Feb. 22 at⁢ the Buffalo Sabres.
“You don’t want to see​ any​ of our ‍players go down with ⁢injuries,” Rangers coach Peter Laviolette said, “but where there is a‍ little bit of time coming up ⁢here, that’s ‌useful. There’s no games being played, so that’s a useful thing.”
Goalie Dylan Garand was recalled from‌ Hartford of the American Hockey ⁣League and backed up Quick on Saturday.
igor Shesterkin’s​ Injury​ Impact on New York Rangers ​ ‌⁤ ⁢ In a recent development, Igor Shesterkin, the New york Rangers’ star ⁢goaltender, has been sidelined with an upper-body injury. ⁢this news has meaningful implications for the team as they prepare ⁣for the upcoming 4 Nations⁢ Face-Off ⁣and ‍subsequent games.
Interview​ with NHL Analyst, Mike Krieger Senior⁤ Editor (SE): Mike,​ thanks for⁤ joining us today. Can you provide⁣ some insights into Igor Shesterkin’s⁤ injury and ​its potential impact⁤ on the⁢ New York Rangers?
Assessing ‍the Injury Mike Krieger (MK): Thanks for having me. Igor‍ Shesterkin​ is undoubtedly ‌a key player for the ‍Rangers. an upper-body⁢ injury, ⁣especially⁤ for a goalie, ⁣can range⁢ widely in‍ severity, but the fact that ⁣he’ll be‌ out for 1-2 weeks suggests it’s not ‌too severe. Though, any injury​ to a ⁣starting goalie is a significant concern.
performance Stats SE: What do you make​ of his season ‍so far? His stats show he’s ‌had a mix of successes and challenges.
MK: Yes, ⁤Shesterkin has had⁢ a solid season despite some fluctuations in ​performance.⁢ With an 18-19-2 record,⁣ a 2.87⁤ goals-against average, and a .906 save percentage, he’s shown he can be a reliable goalie,⁣ but ‌there’s room⁣ for betterment. The three shutouts prove his capability to dominate games.
Jonathan‌ Swift’s Role SE: With​ Shesterkin​ out, Jonathan Quick ⁤will likely ‌see more action. How do you see⁣ him fitting into this adjustment?
MK: Jonathan Quick has​ been a veteran presence and a reliable backup. His performance in the ⁤recent win against‌ the Columbus Blue Jackets ⁢was commendable, making 22‍ saves. He’ll need to step up in Shesterkin’s absence⁤ and provide stability⁢ to prevent any significant drop in performance.
Coach⁢ Laviolette’s Perspective SE: Rangers​ coach Peter Laviolette mentioned that the ⁤timing ⁣of​ the injury could be useful due to the absence of‌ games during the 4​ Nations Face-off. ⁤What’s your take on that?
MK: ⁢ Coach Laviolette’s assessment is spot-on. The break is ‍actually a blessing in⁢ disguise. It allows Shesterkin some time to recuperate ‍without‌ missing game time. It ‍also gives Quick the ​chance to get some more⁣ practice and ensure smooth transitions, minimizing any disruptions‌ when‍ Shesterkin ‌returns.
Dylan Garand’s⁣ Recall SE: Dylan Garand was recalled from the​ Hartford team in the American⁤ Hockey League. What kind of impact do you think he could have?
MK: ⁤Garand’s ‌recall is essential for ⁣depth and provides a backup plan if Quick encounters any issues. Coming from the AHL, he might need ​some ⁢time to acclimatize, but⁤ his presence is crucial for maintaining the goalie rotation and keeping the team⁢ flexible.
Takeaways SE: Mike, what are the‍ main takeaways from this situation⁤ and how shoudl the Rangers⁣ approach this challenge?
MK: The Rangers need to focus on maintaining⁢ their concentration and⁢ teamwork. Quick and garand will need to fill Shesterkin’s shoes temporarily,ensuring they sustain the overall excellence of the team. ​The ‌upcoming break gives them a perfect ‍opportunity‌ to‍ rest and strategize for their return on‍ February 22.
SE: Thanks, Mike, for these ​valuable insights.⁣ It’s‍ been truly informative.
